requirements.text: Experience: At least 1 year of full-time professional software engineering experience building and shipping production systems. Internships are not counted toward this minimum. We are open on level — we care more about what you have built than how long you have been building.
Education: BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Software Engineering. MS preferred. We also consider other STEM degrees alongside a record of shipped production software.
Education: BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Software Engineering. MS preferred. We also consider other STEM degrees alongside a record of shipped production software.
Shipped Software: Demonstrated experience delivering working software end to end — not prototypes or notebooks.

Coding Proficiency: Strong, production-grade Python — the primary language for this team's automation and tooling. Java is expected for senior candidates and preferred for junior ones: our core platform is built in Java, and you will work across both over time. Comfort with shell, and with reading unfamiliar codebases, matters as much as either language.

Cloud and Containers: Experience with AWS and containerization (Docker/Kubernetes).
Built for Others: Evidence of building something other people then used — an internal tool, a library, a plugin, a template, a service another team depends on.
Collaboration and Ownership: Able to work across team boundaries, take end-to-end ownership, and operate where the path is not already defined.
TypeScript — solution features often land in our front end.
LLM-powered agent workflows — LangChain/LangGraph, multi-agent orchestration, tool calling or RAG — for production or internal platforms.
Distributed data frameworks such as Spark, Kafka or Flink.
Experience deploying or maintaining machine learning models in production.
Analytical databases and large-scale data exploration (ClickHouse or other columnar stores).
Real-time decision engines or stateful stream processing.
Domain knowledge in fraud or risk — a plus, never a requirement.
